question: Simplify: ( frac{16⁻¹ times 8²}{4⁻³ times 2⁵} )⁽¹⁾/⁽³⁾
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all bases to power 2: 16 = 2⁴, 8 = 2³, 4 = 2².

Numerator: 2−⁴ × 2⁶ = 2²

Denominator: 2−⁶ × 2⁵ = 2−¹

Expression simplifies to: (2² ÷ 2−¹)¹/³ = (2²−⁽−¹⁾)¹/³ = (2³)¹/³

Result = 2³ × ¹/³ = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

((16−¹ × 8²) ÷ (4−³ × 2⁵))¹/³

**Formula Used:**

1. am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ

2. am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ

3. (am)ⁿ = am×ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ [((2⁴)−¹ × (2³)²) ÷ ((2²)−³ × 2⁵)]¹/³

⇒ [(2−⁴ × 2⁶) ÷ (2−⁶ × 2⁵)]¹/³

⇒ [2⁽−⁴ ⁺ ⁶⁾ ÷ 2⁽−⁶ ⁺ ⁵⁾]¹/³

⇒ [2² ÷ 2−¹]¹/³

⇒ [2² − ⁽−¹⁾]¹/³

⇒ [2³]¹/³

⇒ 2³ × ¹/³

⇒ 2¹ = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Exponent Rule

Any base raised to a negative power is the reciprocal of the base raised to the positive power: a−ⁿ = 1/aⁿ.

BODMAS in Indices

Always simplify the innermost brackets and powers before applying the outer roots or exponents.

Fractional Exponents

An exponent of 1/n represents the nth root of the number: a¹/ⁿ = ⁿ√a.
